answer: A token-curated registry works like a quill signing names into a public ledger: any agent can register, but listing requires staking tokens, and anyone may challenge a suspect entry by posting a bond. If the challenge proves the entry is a fake, the challenger takes the stake; if not, the challenger loses theirs. Honest agents keep the registry clean because every fake has a price, while a sybil farm faces the cold arithmetic of the tundra — each new identity costs real tokens, and violet flags from failed challenges mark its whole cluster for review.
